canopy.silhouette: broad dark dome on short forked trunk

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal: the acorn stays in the soil and first drives down a taproot (about 70 cm in 2 months). The shoot is a thin, reddish, downy stem with small, cupped, glossy, spiny-toothed evergreen leaves. Seedlings grow slowly in the shade of shrubs or grass for years, then form a slender sapling before spreading into a broad dome; it resprouts strongly after fire.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Quercus agrifolia (acorns germinate 15-50 d after falling, no dormancy; taproot ~70 cm in 2 months; slow natural top growth; recruitment best in shade; shade tolerant throughout life; 6-25 m; trees may live over 250 yr); first acorn age estimated

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Quercus agrifolia (catkins Mar-Apr, wind-pollinated; acorns 2.5-3.8 cm, the only California black oak maturing in 1 year, ripen Sep-Oct; most drop in fall, some hang until spring; crop failures ~half of years; scrub jays cache ~5,000 acorns each); acorn meal was leached and cooked

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings have 10-13 cotyledons and for 5-10 years carry juvenile foliage: single, soft, silvery blue-green needles 2-4 cm long, making a bushy, rounded, bluish globe rather than a cone. Adult paired, stiff green needles gradually take over by about age 10; the tree then lifts into a flat umbrella crown on a bare trunk.
growth.source: Wikipedia (juvenile leaves for 5-10 years, fully adult by ~10; a bushy globe in youth, an umbrella in mid-age; 12-20 m typical, to 25+; cones take 36 months to mature, longest of any pine); first cones and lifespan estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (broad ovoid cones 8-15 cm that take 36 months to mature, longer than any other pine; edible nuts 2 cm long with a rudimentary wing); about 29-33 months from spring pollination to ripe cone in the third autumn; crop and decay estimated

canopy.name: Mediterranean cypress

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal, with slender cotyledons; the first shoots bear small, spreading needle-like juvenile leaves before the dark green, appressed scale leaves take over. Fast-growing when young: a dense, narrow cone of upswept branches (a slim column in the fastigiate form, which is what most planted trees are; wild trees spread horizontally).
growth.source: conifers.org (20-30 m, fast-growing when young, seeds from its tenth year, up to 1000 yr; cones 2-3 cm, 8-14 scales, serotinous); Wikipedia (to 35 m, >1000 yr, Sarv-e Abarkuh estimated ~4000 yr); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (cones ripen second year, 64-280 seeds, 28-d germination test)

canopy.source: E Mediterranean hills; the dark column of graveyards and ruins. Kew POWO.

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal: the acorn stays in the soil; a slender stem appears with small, toothed, dark evergreen leaves, grey-felted beneath. Within a few years the bark begins thickening into pale, spongy, deeply fissured cork. Saplings grow best sheltered by shrubs but need more light later; the first 'virgin' cork is stripped when the tree is about 25 years old.
growth.source: European Atlas of Forest Tree Species (Quercus suber: usually 20 m, to 25 m; slow-growing; about 200 yr or more); Wikipedia (10-15 m typical; first cork harvest at ~25 yr, then every 9-12 yr; trees can live over 400 yr); growth curve, shade and first acorns estimated

fruiting.source: European Atlas of Forest Tree Species (flowers from April through summer; both annual and biennial acorns, 2-3 cm, fairly deep cup with long scales); Wikipedia (acorns 2-4.5 cm, bare, smooth, shiny brownish-red; 15-30 kg of acorns per tree per year)

shrub.silhouette: open grey-green shrub on red twisting stems

growth.juvenile_note: After a fire, seedlings come up en masse with the first winter rains: two small round cotyledons, then stiff, pale blue-grey, round-oval leaves held edge-on to the sun on a single reddish stem. It branches into a bushy rounded shrub, and the smooth red-purple bark and twisting limbs of the adult show within a few years. It has no burl, so fire kills it.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Arctostaphylos glauca: shrub 1 to over 6 m; seeds need fire to germinate; long-lived, 100+ yr, but does not fruit until about 20 yr old; reproduces by seed and layering). Chaparral seedling ecology from USDA FEIS (Arctostaphylos glandulosa). Germination days and height-age estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (hanging clusters of narrow urn-shaped white flowers; drupe 12-15 mm, light red, thick pulp in a tough sticky coat, 3-6 nutlets fused into one stone; eaten and made into cider). Winter flowering months, pollinators (bees, hummingbirds), timings and crop estimated from Jepson as recalled and FEIS manzanita accounts.

shrub.silhouette: dense dark wiry shrub, many upright stems

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings come up in the first rains after a fire: a thin stem with tiny needle-like leaves in little bundles. By year 2 a small woody lignotuber forms at the root crown. Most young plants seen are resprouts instead: dozens (up to 500) of straight, wand-like green shoots from the burned burl, about 50 cm tall after one season.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Adenostoma fasciculatum (heat- and charate-stimulated germination in the first rainy season after fire; ~90% first-year seedling mortality; seed by ~3 yr; sprouts 50 cm yr 1, 85 cm yr 5, 1 m yr 20; lives 100-200 yr; shade intolerant)

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Adenostoma fasciculatum (white flowers in showy 2.5-10 cm terminal clusters on current growth in June; fruit develops in July; ripening and dispersal complete by August; achenes; seed output rises with shrub age); pollinators estimated (generalist insects)

ground.silhouette: grey strap rosette with tall branched flower spike

growth.juvenile_note: Three-angled black seeds sprout after the autumn rains. The seedling shows one grass-like leaf, then a small tuft of flat, keeled, narrowly triangular grey-green leaves over a cluster of swelling spindle-shaped root tubers. Leaves wither in the summer drought and regrow each autumn; after 2-4 years the clump sends up a branched spike of white, brown-veined star flowers.
growth.source: Useful Temperate Plants (theferns.info): seed germinates in 1-3 months at 15 C, rosettes of leaves to 40 cm, flowering stems to 1.2 m, dry rocky hills; Pacific Bulb Society (Asphodelus); age at first flowering and lifespan estimated for a tuberous-rooted geophyte.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two tiny rounded cotyledons, then minute paired grey-green leaves on a thread-thin square stem. It branches from the base within months into a small aromatic sprig and in 2-3 years becomes a dense, woody, grey-green cushion of wiry stems with tiny rolled-edged leaves, covered in whorls of pale pink to mauve flowers in late spring.
growth.source: Wikipedia Thymus vulgaris (15-30 cm tall, ~40 cm wide; purple or pink flowers in early summer; western Mediterranean to S Italy); NC State Extension (15-30 cm x 15-40 cm, blooms May-Jul, full sun, bees and butterflies, uneven seed germination). Germination days, first flowering and lifespan estimated from herb growers.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings come up with the first autumn-winter rains after a fire, in even-aged crowds. Epigeal: two fleshy, oval cotyledons, then a single upright stem with narrow, hairless, bright green leaves; it branches after a year or two into a dense, upright shrub. Adults are killed by fire and restock only from seed held in the old, closed brown flowerheads.
growth.source: SANBI PlantZAfrica (1-4.5 m; germinates 3-4 weeks after sowing in autumn; first flowers about 4-5 yr from seed; semi-serotinous; ~20% of flowers set seed; bird and beetle pollinated; fires every 10-30 yr); Wikipedia (reseeder killed by fire). Lifespan estimated.
